title: Whitened norm for opposite signs
statement: Let $-1<\rho<1$, let $c\in\mathbb{R}$, and let $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}$. For the matrix $\Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}1&\rho\\\rho&1\end{pmatrix}$, the Euclidean norm of $\Sigma^{-1/2}(\varepsilon c,-\varepsilon c)$ is at most $\sqrt{2}\,|c|/\sqrt{1-\rho}$, where $\Sigma^{-1/2}$ denotes the inverse of the positive square root of $\Sigma$.
